newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products - gasoline soars, rest firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products - gasoline soars, rest firmer.

text.p: NWE oil products were in most cases slightly higher on Monday, while gasoline prompt values jumped by around $12 on the back of refinery woes.

Gasoline prompt barges for first half August jumped on the back of Friday's news of three cat cracker outages and despite Monday's confirmed return to normal production at the BP/Texaco Nerefco unit in Rotterdam.
The $12 jump was confirmed by a string of trades at $227 as cargoes were also seen dramatically higher amid rumors of a $231 CIF NWE prompt to mid-August trade for 10,000 tonnes of gasoline.
Backwardation widened considerably, however, with second half August Eurograde barges seen just $4 up, August swaps up by $7 and September by $2.50-$3.
The mogas jump, while helping to keep naphtha physical values stable and August swap quotes $1-$2 higher, raised the mogas/naphtha front-month spread to $25-plus.
Brokers said this had yet to encourage significant new interest in naphthenic and aromatic naphtha for gasoline production.
Rumoured petchem cracker problems at Tarragona, Spain, and Terneuzen, Netherlands, were meanwhile seen furher limiting already lackluster demand for paraffinic naphtha.
Gas oil was narrowly firmer on the back of a 75 cent gain on IPE futures, but differentials were essentially unchanged.
High sulphur fuel oil barges firmed a little to trade at $94 and $94.25 fob ARA with two majors said to be having some loading problems causing a shortage of supplies.
High sulphur fuel cargoes were a mixed bag with some traders putting them at about $88/$89 cif and others a few dollars lower but no trades were heard early in the day to back up either side.
